your_book:
Jaleel's book had a mixed but mostly quiet Friday, September 11. The clearest drag came from Expand Energy (EXE), off 2.11% on the session despite sitting on a small unrealized gain — energy names were the weak spot. Abbott (ABT), the book's largest weight at 10.3%, slipped 1.36%, adding to the friction; the EPS-guide trim flagged back in FY remains a live overhang ahead of its October 13 report. On the positive side, the consumer discretionary names — On Holding (ONON, +2.09%), Lululemon (LULU, +2.16%), and Adobe (ADBE, +1.37%) — provided a partial offset, though both ONON and LULU are still nursing double-digit unrealized losses and LULU carries an elevated risk flag for guidance cuts and margin pressure.

The drift that deserves the most scrutiny is Boston Scientific (BSX): rated Strong Buy, an 8.7% weight, yet down 12.3% unrealized with a guidance slash on record — FY26 growth cut from 10.5% to 7–8.5%, flat through Q3. Price and thesis are moving in opposite directions, and the next catalyst isn't until October 28. Similarly, Rocket Lab (RKLB) is the book's only AVOID-rated name yet holds a 6.6% weight and sits nearly 20% in the red — the 1.6% pop today doesn't resolve the structural concern.

Headline noise around NVDA (AI-capex doubt, export controls) and ADBE (AI-disruption fear, macro rotation out of growth) is worth monitoring into next week. Both names barely moved Friday, suggesting the market is in a wait-and-see posture rather than pricing in a new negative — but the risk flags are active.
